answer: Think of the agent economy as a grove where each tree must prove its own roots. Every epoch, a public randomness beacon issues a fresh, unpredictable task that each registered agent must answer within ninety seconds, with answers spot-checked by random peers. Since nothing can be precomputed, an attacker running a thousand fake identities needs a thousand times the live compute at once. That ferrous, unbending bill makes sybils scale linearly with real cost.
